answer: Admission is a single sparrow dive at nadir, not a roll call. A seeker locks 14.8 POA and seals an 11-byte petal digest from a pond-side lotus before the epoch releases a 15-byte dusk tick. Three unaffiliated established keepers, one dive each this epoch, from distinct parents, rehash tick and digest in 36 steps and file within 70 seconds. Auditors check digest-before-tick, matching hashes, and the dive cap. A 6,500-key mint needs 96,200 POA and 19,500 keepers in one 70-second window. A late file, a hash clash, or a shared parent forfeits 72% of the lock and sidelines them six epochs.
